Lately, though, things have gotten strange. I've been hearing these whispers, like people talking about me when no one's there, and I feel like sometimes the TV is sending me secret messages. There have been times, especially when I’m really stressed, that I’ve experienced some strange things, like hearing faint whispers or feeling like people are staring at me more than usual, but the constant feeling of needing to move, the blurting out, that's just always been a part of me, long before any of these other… fleeting experiences started. Even when I’m on set, trying to focus on a scene, I find myself getting up and pacing, or just feeling this intense restlessness. My ex-wife used to get so frustrated with me, said I was always "on the go," like a motor that wouldn't shut off, and that was long before things got really strange.

I’m always buzzing, like a motor is running inside me; I just can’t sit still, even in meetings. I’ll blurt things out, cutting people off without meaning to, or even just walk out of a conversation to pace. It’s been like this since I was a kid; my teachers always commented on my being fidgety and easily distracted.

And the ideas… they just race. It’s hard to keep track of a single train of thought, and then organizing a shoot feels almost impossible. I lose things, miss deadlines, and my assistant is constantly reminding me of commitments. On top of that, there are times lately, especially when I’m really stressed from the constant push to keep up, when I’ll hear faint whispers or see fleeting shadows in my peripheral vision—nothing clear or threatening, just enough to be unsettling. But those don't start the restlessness or the buzzing, that’s always been with me, long before I started experiencing anything like that. It’s honestly exhausting.

Before that, I was always pretty focused, intense even, but this feeling of being "driven by a motor" and unable to follow through? That’s new, and it happened right around the time these other… sensory experiences began. I feel like I'm constantly on the go, but achieving nothing."
